sections.h2: Where in Clinton County are deeds filed?
sections.html:
Take it to the courthouse in St. Johns. The land records for Clinton County are kept by an office that combines the county clerk and the register of deeds, found at 100 E State Street, Suite 2500, with a phone line at 989-224-5270.

The doors are open on weekdays from eight until noon, then again from one until five. Staff ask that you walk in by 4:30 so a transaction is not rushed at closing time, and holiday schedules can shift. Passport services run from the same office by appointment only.

Do not expect the counter to help you write anything. Employees do not prepare or alter documents, do not give legal advice, and keep no blank deeds in stock. For a sale, a title company or attorney writes the deed and sends it over.

sections.h2: What will recording a Clinton County deed cost me?
sections.html:
Thirty dollars flat, whatever the page count. That is the charge for a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens, and the county's recording fees page lists the same figure alongside the add-ons below.

Charges the Clinton County office may add to a closing package
ItemChargeSource
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30 eachMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Release or assignment naming extra instruments$3 per extra instrument namedMCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Stamp certifying a recorded paper$5MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
Photocopy$1 a pageMCL 600.2567(1)(c)
Treasurer's tax certificate$5 for 25 descriptions, 20 cents more for each beyondClinton County Register of Deeds

If you ask staff to search the index for you, the statutory rate is fifty cents per year covered, never less than $5.

sections.h2: Which formatting mistakes get a Clinton County deed sent back?
sections.html:
The county posts a sixteen-point checklist drawn from Michigan's recording statutes, and the office will look over a draft before you file it. Common reasons for rejection, in the county's own words, are an incorrect fee, no drafter named, names not typed under the signatures, a male grantor's marital status left out, and an unfinished notary block.

  • Reserve a 2.5-inch blank strip across the top of page one and half an inch on every other edge.
  • Print in black ink, ten-point type or bigger, on white paper no lighter than 20-pound stock, cut between letter and legal size.
  • Open the first printed line with a statement naming the single event the paper records, such as a warranty deed. A paper that combines two events is refused.
  • Give each party's street address, plus the name and address of whoever drafted the deed.
  • Truncate any Social Security number to its final four digits.
  • Lift the legal description from the previous deed or a fresh survey instead of the abbreviated wording on an assessment notice.

A survivor deed must come with a certified death certificate, unless the certificate is already recorded and the deed cites its liber and page. A court order has to arrive as a certified copy bearing the court clerk's seal.

sections.h2: Who owes transfer tax on a Clinton County sale, and how much?
sections.html:
The seller does, in two layers. The state layer is $3.75 and the county layer is 55 cents, each applied per $500 slice of price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full slice (MCL 207.504 and 207.523).

Work it through for a $250,000 house. That price holds 500 slices, so the state takes $1,875 and the county $275, for $2,150 total. Typically the title company deducts it from the seller's proceeds. The county treasurer collects it, and the statute allows 15 days from delivery of the deed.

  • Outside both taxes: any deed carrying less than $100 of value, and deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Outside the state tax: transfers in foreclosure or by deed in lieu, and gifts from a parent to a child or from a grandparent to a grandchild (MCL 207.526).
  • The county statute lists no family exemption of its own, so ask the register how the county layer is treated on a family transfer.

Print any exemption claim on the deed itself. If none appears, the clerk charges the tax at the window.

sections.h2: When does a Clinton County deed need the treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
Whenever it is a warranty deed, any other deed with warranty language, a land contract, or an assignment of a land contract that carries a warranty clause. Under MCL 211.135 the register may not record those papers until the county treasurer has certified the parcel's tax status.

The certificate reaches back five years before the instrument's date and reports any tax liens or tax titles. A quitclaim without warranty covenants skips the step. For a seller who is behind on taxes, request a payoff letter from the Clinton County Treasurer early, so the balance can be paid at closing and the certificate comes back without a lien.

sections.h2: What does the Clinton County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
This is Lansing's northern commuter belt. On QuickFacts the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $259,500 and the typical household earns $88,210. Owners live in 82.2% of occupied homes. Renters pay $1,092 at the median, and the county issued 197 building permits during 2025.

The county dates to 1831, was organized in 1839 and honors DeWitt Clinton. It spans 566 square miles of land and holds the cities of St. Johns, DeWitt, and parts of Ovid, Lansing, East Lansing and Grand Ledge. Interstate 69 crosses the south, US 127 passes through St. Johns and DeWitt, and M-21 links Fowler, St. Johns and Ovid.

The 2020 count was 79,128 people. A July 2025 estimate puts it at 80,432, a 1.6% rise. Residents tend to stay: 89.7% lived at the same address a year earlier, which means a house for sale often draws buyers from outside the neighborhood rather than from next door.

sections.h2: How has Clinton County grown, and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Growth is the story here. The county counted 37,969 people in 1960, 57,883 in 1990 and 75,382 in 2010 before reaching 79,128 in 2020. Most of that came as Lansing's suburbs pushed north, and DeWitt Township holds Capital Region International Airport, just off I-69.

The county belongs to the Lansing-East Lansing metropolitan area, and about 48.7% of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census, with the rest in rural townships. Census-designated places such as Bath, Eureka, Lake Victoria and Wacousta sit alongside the cities, so a Clinton County address can mean anything from a subdivision lot near DeWitt to farmland beyond St. Johns.

Those differences matter at sale time. A house on a rural parcel may involve a private well and septic system, a legal description that spans acreage, and a survey, while a city lot usually comes with a short platted description. In either case the register of deeds only needs the recorded instrument to meet the format list above. QuickFacts also shows 95.3% of adults with a high school diploma and 35.4% with a bachelor's degree, and 63.8% of people 16 and older in the labor force.

sections.h2: What happens at closing when a Clinton County owner sells for cash?
sections.html:
The paperwork matches a financed sale. The closing agent submits the signed deed to the register with the $30 fee, adds a treasurer's certificate if the deed warrants title, and attaches either the transfer tax or the exemption wording.

Before you sign, ask who is ordering the certificate, whether the deed recites the full price or relies on a valuation affidavit, and what exemption, if any, is claimed. If you mail originals yourself, enclose a stamped return envelope so the recorded deed comes back to you.

One more errand sits outside the register's counter. The new owner has 45 days to file a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor. A seller who had claimed the principal residence exemption files to end it as of the closing date.

faqs.q: How much is the Clinton County filing fee for a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars, charged per document. Expect an extra $5 for the treasurer's certificate on a warranty deed, which covers up to 25 legal descriptions.

faqs.q: Is the buyer or the seller responsible for transfer tax in St. Johns or DeWitt?
faqs.a: The seller. The statutes name the grantor as the liable party, and the title company usually withholds the tax from what the seller receives.

faqs.q: Will courthouse staff prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. They review drafts against the recording rules but leave the writing to an attorney, a lender or a title company.

faqs.q: Can I drop off a deed over the lunch hour?
faqs.a: Not in person. The office shuts from noon to one on weekdays. Phone 989-224-5270 to check holiday schedules.

faqs.q: Why did the register send my deed back?
faqs.a: The usual culprits are a wrong fee, a missing drafter name, signatures with no typed names beneath, a half-finished notary block, thin margins, or two recordable events on one paper.
